precepts.text: Gamaliel warned the council with examples: Theudas boasted himself to be somebody and four hundred joined him, and he was slain and all who obeyed him scattered; Judas of Galilee drew away much people, and he perished and all who obeyed him were dispersed.
precepts.point: Moses said if these men die the common death of all men, the Lord hath not sent me; but if the earth open her mouth and swallow them up, then ye shall understand that these men have provoked the Lord. The ground clave asunder, they and their houses and goods went down alive into the pit, all Israel fled at their cry, and fire from the Lord consumed the two hundred and fifty. These things were written for our learning about leaders.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
Korah, Dathan, Abiram and On “took men”, “two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown”. They were not nobodies; they had a name, and what they had was influence over the congregation. They used it against Moses and Aaron: “Ye take too much upon you”. And the results of those leaders: the earth “swallowed them up, and their houses, and all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods”, and fire from the Lord “consumed the two hundred and fifty men that offered incense.” Everyone who followed them went down with them.

These things were written aforetime for our learning, and Acts 5 shows the same lesson. The apostles were brought before the council, and Gamaliel stood up and warned them: “Ye men of Israel, take heed to yourselves what ye intend to do as touching these men.” Then he gave examples.

“For before these days rose up Theudas, boasting himself to be somebody; to whom a number of men, about four hundred, joined themselves”. Four hundred men joined themselves to a man who came across as a leader, and he “was slain; and all, as many as obeyed him, were scattered, and brought to nought.” Then “rose up Judas of Galilee in the days of the taxing, and drew away much people after him: he also perished; and all, even as many as obeyed him, were dispersed.”

That is the pattern with false leaders: the leader perishes, and the ones that obeyed him perish and are scattered with him, just like the men that appertained unto Korah. “For the leaders of this people cause them to err; and they that are led of them are destroyed.” The leaders of the black community today, the Christian pastors, have our people living in hell, with drugs, gang violence, shootings on the block and adultery, and those that follow them are destroyed with them.

precepts.text: Two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly gathered against Moses and Aaron, saying all the congregation are holy, wherefore lift ye up yourselves.
precepts.point: Moses set the proof before them: if these men die the common death of all men, the Lord hath not sent me; but if the Lord make a new thing and the earth open her mouth and swallow them, then ye shall understand that these men have provoked the Lord.

note.label: Deuteronomy 11: Remember His Acts, Keep His Commandments

precepts.why:
What the Lord did unto Dathan and Abiram is the rebellion of Korah in Numbers 16. “And they rose up before Moses, with certain of the children of Israel, two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown”. Not nobodies: princes, famous, men of renown. And they told Moses and Aaron, “Ye take too much upon you, seeing all the congregation are holy, every one of them, and the Lord is among them: wherefore then lift ye up yourselves above the congregation of the Lord?”

The same spirits are back on the earth today. They come into the congregation, and after a season they rise up thinking themselves wiser than the leadership, the bishop and the deacons: ye take too much upon you, all the congregation is holy. Nothing new under the sun. Moses set Israel to remember what happened to Dathan and Abiram so that spirit would be known for what it is.

precepts.text: Hereby ye shall know the Lord hath sent me: if the Lord make a new thing and the earth open her mouth and swallow them, these men have provoked the Lord.
precepts.point: Moses set the proof before them: if these men die the common death of all men, the Lord hath not sent me; but if the Lord make a new thing and the earth open her mouth and swallow them, then ye shall understand that these men have provoked the Lord.

note.label: Deuteronomy 11: Remember His Acts, Keep His Commandments

precepts.why:
Moses set the proof before them: “Hereby ye shall know that the Lord hath sent me to do all these works; for I have not done them of mine own mind. If these men die the common death of all men, or if they be visited after the visitation of all men; then the Lord hath not sent me.” He put it in the Lord's hands to show who he had sent.

“But if the Lord make a new thing, and the earth open her mouth, and swallow them up, with all that appertain unto them, and they go down quick into the pit; then ye shall understand that these men have provoked the Lord.” Whether Moses and Aaron took too much upon them was going to be answered by the Lord, not by the princes. That is what Moses tells Israel to remember: “how the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up”, in the midst of all Israel, and their eyes saw it.

precepts.text: The earth opened her mouth and swallowed them up, and they went down alive into the pit, and perished from among the congregation.
precepts.point: Moses set the proof before them: if these men die the common death of all men, the Lord hath not sent me; but if the Lord make a new thing and the earth open her mouth and swallow them, then ye shall understand that these men have provoked the Lord.

note.label: Deuteronomy 11: Remember His Acts, Keep His Commandments

precepts.why:
“And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and their houses, and all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods. They, and all that appertained to them, went down alive into the pit, and the earth closed upon them: and they perished from among the congregation.” The new thing Moses spoke of came to pass exactly as he said it, so all Israel understood that those men had provoked the Lord.

That is the history behind Moses' words: “how the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and their households, and their tents, and all the substance that was in their possession, in the midst of all Israel”. Their households and all their substance went down with them. “But your eyes have seen all the great acts of the Lord which he did.” The generation Moses is speaking to saw it, and the same spirits that rise up against the bishop and the deacons today should remember how the Lord answered that rebellion.

precepts.text: The rebels called the land Israel came out of a land that floweth with milk and honey; that land was Egypt.
precepts.point: The honey teaching carries a dietary lesson: hast thou found honey, eat so much as is sufficient for thee. Do not overeat; balance your salts, sugars, meats, and dainties moderately.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
“a land that floweth with milk and honey.” The Bible's own dictionary, precept upon precept, tells what that means. The rebels said to Moses, “Is it a small thing that thou hast brought us up out of a land that floweth with milk and honey, to kill us in the wilderness”. The land they were brought up out of was Egypt; so the rebels called Egypt the land flowing with milk and honey.

So the phrase describes a land abundant in food. The milk goes into your cattle and your meats, and the honey goes into your vegetation.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

points: Korah, Dathan and Abiram, famous men in the congregation, rose up against Moses and Aaron, saying ye take too much upon you. Their rebellion was not overnight.
Moses asked if it was a small thing that God had separated them to his service. They were not satisfied and wanted the priesthood.
The earth swallowed them and fire consumed the 250 princes. Rising against the men God sent is rising against God.

Korah was of Levi, and Dathan, Abiram, and On were of Reuben. With them rose up two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown; that is two hundred and fifty three in all against Moses and Aaron.
These were known and powerful men among the congregation, and their influence, because of who they were, is how they were able to persuade people.

They charged Moses and Aaron with taking too much upon themselves and lifting themselves above the congregation. They thought Moses and Aaron carried themselves as better than the rest, but the Most High is the one who chose them as leaders and was dealing with them; the accusers were jealous of them.

When Moses heard it, he fell upon his face, and told Korah and all his company: even to morrow the Lord will shew who are his, and who is holy; the Most High himself would show whom he chose and whom he was dealing with.

The test was censers: take you censers, Korah and all his company, put fire therein and incense before the Lord, and the man whom the Lord doth choose, he shall be holy. Ye take too much upon you, ye sons of Levi.

Moses exhorted Korah: seemeth it but a small thing that the God of Israel hath separated you from the congregation to bring you near to himself, to do the service of the tabernacle? Only Levi could do the service of the tabernacle, and that was a heavy job in itself.

You already stand before the congregation and minister unto them; the Most High is still dealing with you. But they sought the priesthood also, and for that cause Korah and all his company were gathered together against the Lord: and what is Aaron, that ye murmur against him?

Dathan and Abiram would not come up when Moses called them. They were being rebellious against Moses because they wanted his spot, accusing him of bringing them out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill them in the wilderness and of making himself a prince over them.
Moses was very wroth and said unto the Lord, respect not thou their offering: I have not taken one ass from them, neither have I hurt one of them.

Every man took his censer, two hundred and fifty censers, with Aaron and Korah also, put fire and incense in them, and stood in the door of the tabernacle of the congregation; and Korah gathered all the congregation against Moses and Aaron, and the glory of the Lord appeared unto all the congregation.
The Lord told Moses and Aaron to separate themselves from among the congregation, that he might consume them in a moment: get away from them, because judgment is about to come.

Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces and pleaded: O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and wilt thou be wroth with all the congregation? They still had that love for their people and pleaded with the Lord not to deal with the whole congregation over one man's sin.

The Lord commanded the congregation to get up from about the tabernacle of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram; Moses warned them to depart from the tents of these wicked men and touch nothing of theirs, lest they be consumed in all their sins and put to death in all that wickedness.

The congregation got up from the tabernacle of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram on every side; and Dathan and Abiram came out and stood in the door of their tents with their wives, their sons, and their little children.

Moses put the proof on the Most High: hereby ye shall know that the Lord hath sent me to do all these works, for I have not done them of mine own mind. If these men die the common death of all men, then the Lord hath not sent me; if the Most High does not do something out of the ordinary to put them to death, then the Lord had not sent him.
But if the Lord make a new thing, and the earth open her mouth and swallow them up, and they go down quick into the pit, then ye shall understand that these men have provoked the Lord.

As he made an end of speaking, the ground clave asunder under them, and the earth opened her mouth and swallowed them up, their houses, all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods; anybody that had something to do with them went down, with all they owned.

The earth just opened and closed upon them, and they perished from among the congregation; all Israel round about fled at the cry of them, for you could hear them crying as they were swallowed up, and they said, lest the earth swallow us up also.
The other two hundred and fifty men that followed them and offered incense did not escape either: there came out a fire from the Lord and consumed them.

The Lord told Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest to take up the censers out of the burning, for they are hallowed, and scatter the fire yonder; the censers of these sinners against their own souls were made broad plates for a covering of the altar, because they were offered before the Lord.

The plates were a memorial and a sign unto the children of Israel, that no stranger which is not of the seed of Aaron come near to offer incense before the Lord, that he be not as Korah and as his company.

On the morrow, the very next day, all the congregation murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying, ye have killed the people of the Lord. After they had just seen the earth open up and swallow men, they still would not let it go and gathered against Moses again; that is just how rebellious we are.

The Most High saw what was going on, and the cloud covered the tabernacle and the glory of the Lord appeared; Moses and Aaron came before the tabernacle because they knew the Most High was ready to deal with them.

The Lord came down ready to put them to death again, saying get you up from among this congregation, that I may consume them as in a moment; and Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces, still pleading for their people because they loved them so much.

Moses told Aaron to take a censer with fire from off the altar and incense, and go quickly unto the congregation and make an atonement for them, for wrath had gone out from the Lord and the plague was begun; the Most High was already putting them to death.
Aaron ran into the midst of the congregation, put on incense, made an atonement for the people, and stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed.

They that died in the plague were fourteen thousand and seven hundred, beside them that died about the matter of Korah; so beside the two hundred and fifty three that died with Korah, fourteen thousand seven hundred more were put to death.
